beats.text: Optimization starts by translating constraints. A rectangle with perimeter twenty has side lengths whose sum is ten. Naming one side x makes the other ten minus x, so one variable now determines the entire area.

The area is x times ten minus x, with nonnegative side lengths restricting x between zero and ten. Expanding gives ten x minus x squared. Its graph shows that increasing one side eventually sacrifices too much of the other.

Differentiate to locate the interior stationary point. Ten minus two x equals zero when x is five. That produces a five by five square with area twenty-five, while either endpoint gives a degenerate rectangle with zero area.

Completing the square explains why this is the global maximum: a square is never negative, so subtracting it cannot exceed twenty-five. A zero derivative only suggests a candidate; the domain and comparison establish what kind of optimum it is.

practice.prompt: A rectangle has perimeter 28. Write its area using one side x, find its maximum, and explain why the answer is a square.
practice.answer: The other side is 14−x, with 0≤x≤14. A=14x−x²=49−(x−7)², so the maximum is 49 at x=7 and y=7.

practice.prompt: Two nonnegative numbers have sum 12. Find their largest possible product and justify the result algebraically or with calculus.
practice.answer: Let them be x and 12−x. Their product is 36−(x−6)²≤36. Equality occurs at 6 and 6.

practice.prompt: The derivative of f(x)=x² is zero at x=0. Explain why this does not make zero a maximum.
practice.answer: f(x)=x²≥0 with equality at 0, so zero is a global minimum. A stationary point can be a minimum, maximum, or neither; classification needs additional reasoning.

takeaway: Write the constraint, respect the domain, find candidates, and justify the optimum rather than trusting a zero derivative alone.
scope: One-variable constrained rectangle optimization with both calculus and completing-the-square justification.
title: Optimization
objective: Model an objective and constraints, compare candidates, and interpret endpoints.
